analysis_steps.goal: Image and mask the CO cube

method.value: CASA clean with natural weighting, then 6'' smoothed 2.5-sigma mask with two-channel continuity, primary-beam correction, subcube

evidence.quote: The result was applied as a blanking mask to the original cube, and after correcting for primary-beam attentuation, we took a $551 \times 301$ pixel $\times 64$ channel subcube

analysis_steps.goal: Make moment maps and convert to column density

method.value: Moment maps from subcube; blank where I(CO) <= 200 Jy/beam m/s; N(H2) from X_CO

evidence.quote: We also blanked the image of the intensity-weighted velocity field and the velocity dispersion image where the CO surface brightness $I{\rm (CO)} \leq 200$ Jybeam$^{-1}$ ms$^{-1}$
we take $X_{CO}$ = $1.8 \pm 0.3 \times 10^{20}$ (H$_2$ cm$^{-2}$)/(K km s$^{-1}$) from (cite: dame01)

analysis_steps.goal: Measure velocity differences across eyelids in face-on polar coordinates

method.value: Deproject with PA = 65 deg, i = 40 deg, nucleus center; measure Δv between outer and inner edges at fixed θ, averaged over 4 pixels (9.3 deg); dv/dR = Δv/(sin i)/ΔR

evidence.quote: We then averaged our measurements over four pixels ($9.3\ensuremath{^\circ}$) in $\theta$ as that gives an arclength $R \Delta \theta$ approximately equal to the FWHM of the PSF

key_parameters.value: eyelid edge at I(CO) = 200 Jy/beam m/s; minimum Δv uncertainty 7 km/s

evidence.quote: Given the channel width, the minimum uncertainty in $\Delta v$ is 7 km s$^{-1}$.

assumptions.value: Δv_z negligible across the eyelid width (nearly in-plane perturbation)

evidence.quote: we assume that across the eyelid width, $\Delta v_z$ for the molecular gas is negligible compared to $\Delta v_R$ or $\Delta v_t$

findings_qualitative.value: Gas in the eyelids shows large velocity gradients with sense consistent with inflow from the outer disk and a pileup.

evidence.quote: The sense of the radial streaming in the eyelids is consistent with the idea that gas from the outer part of IC 2163 flows inward

claims.hypothesis: Gas streams inward and piles up in the eyelids of IC 2163
claims.experiment: Measure CO velocity differences between outer and inner eyelid edges in face-on polar coordinates
claims.result: |Δv| exceeds 100 km/s at some azimuths; sign consistent with inward streaming
claims.finding: Observed velocity field is consistent with inflow and abrupt slowing producing the eyelid pileup

evidence.quote: Thus the observed CO velocity field is consistent with the idea that gas from the outer part of IC 2163 flows inward

claims.hypothesis: Column density correlates with velocity gradient across the eyelids

evidence.quote: The correlation coefficient is 0.84 with 23 degrees of freedom, and thus there is a strong correlation.

claims.hypothesis: Eyelids have elevated turbulence not caused by stellar feedback
claims.experiment: Velocity dispersion maps compared with 24 μm and Halpha clumps
claims.result: High corrected dispersion (~34-37 km/s) on much of the eyelids, not tied to bright clumps
claims.finding: Turbulence from the ocular shock front remains a viable explanation

evidence.quote: Turbulence generated by the ocular shock front remains as a viable explanation for the high values of $(\sigma_v)_{\rm corr}$ on much of the eyelids.

why_this_data.value: HI resolution of 13.5''x12'' is too coarse for the ~6'' eyelid width; ALMA CO resolves outer and inner edges.

evidence.quote: the spatial resolution afforded by the ALMA CO observations allows us to distinguish between the outer and the inner edges of each eyelid

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Inner eyelid edge moving outward was considered as an alternative; checked against v_sys. Northern consistent, southern inner edge appears to move outward.

evidence.quote: an alternative interpretation would have the inner edge of the eyelids moving outwards with respect to the outer edge.

limitations_admitted.value: Missing short spacings could underestimate CO flux; data could not be combined with single-dish.

evidence.quote: The missing short-spacing data in our ALMA maps could lead to underestimates of the total CO flux of each galaxy.

limitations_admitted.value: Cannot separate direct radial impact from shear-driven shocks.

evidence.quote: we are unable to disentangle how much of the observed correlation in Figure [7](#fig7) is due to direct radial impact

referee_caveats_inferred: Constant X_CO assumed in a shocked, possibly turbulent region
Regression is dominated by the northern eyelid; points at neighbouring azimuths are not independent given beam averaging
No pre-eyelid density measured, so the shear-density relation is untested quantitatively
Mixing radial and tangential streaming with a single inclination
